title: Silent degraded defaults in observability export, sandbox manager and guardrail adapters (low-severity fallbacks)
affected_invariant: FRZ-REL-07 / env-vendor rule: missing mandatory configuration fails closed
impact: OTLP profile with empty endpoint drops telemetry silently (distributed OTLP raises); Tier-1 executors default to a relative build/sandbox_sessions manager; guardrail vendors fall back to a regex scanner (audit_payload engine=pattern shows it). Each is bounded: export is derived evidence, isolation is a separate injected authority, degradation is visible in the payload.
recommendation: Make an enabled OTLP profile without endpoint fail at composition (as distributed OTLP does); require an explicit sandbox manager in STRICT; surface guardrail engine downgrade as a typed signal. Record as accepted limitation if intentional.

title: No canonical architecture owner document for Security, sandbox and data lifecycle
affected_invariant: FRZ-CTL-01 (Security one owner) and domain doc pair rule (AGENTS.md)
impact: No docs/project/architecture/ security domain doc and no maintainers/plans pair exist at the baseline; the satellite states it holds no authority and defers to owner documents, which are ADR/threat-model records. FRZ-CTL-01 is PASS while all FRZ-SEC rows are OPEN, so the 'one owner' claim has no single semantic document to anchor it. A code owner exists (runtime/security, runtime/sandbox, application_security_wiring).
recommendation: Owner decision: designate a SECURITY (and sandbox/data lifecycle) architecture doc + plan pair, or record the ADR set as the canonical owner in the doc map.

title: Dormant and duplicate retry-budget mechanisms next to the active inline budget
affected_invariant: FRZ-REL-02 retry ownership explicit; FRZ-CTL-02 reliability one owner
impact: Only the inline budget in llm_adapters/_shared/resilience.py is active in product code; LocalProviderRetryBudget has no production composition (port setter never called outside tests) and StepRetryBudget is referenced only by tests. Retries stay bounded per logical call, so no infinite retry was seen, but a dormant second mechanism can be mistaken for the qualified one in W2-C/HARNESS-W4 evidence. Grep scope: intergrax, agents, applications (docker contexts excluded).
recommendation: Wire LocalProviderRetryBudget at the host composition root or retire it; clarify in FRZ-REL-02 evidence which mechanism is qualified.

title: Product capacity wiring substitutes in-memory Kubernetes scaler and intent-only Celery adapter when URL is unset
affected_invariant: FRZ-REL-07 no hidden fallback; env-vendor rule: missing mandatory config fails closed; ELASTIC doc 'no silent success'
impact: With production_adapters_enabled=True (PRODUCT preset) and INTERGRAX_KUBERNETES_URL unset, capacity mutations succeed against an in-memory scaler seeded nexus-host=2; Celery scaling is always an in-memory counter. The probe can report passed without any cluster. kubernetes_backend='in_memory' is exposed but no non-test consumer rejects or reports it. The doc discloses the in-memory scaler as CI-only and bounds maturity, but its 'no silent success' statement is not what product wiring does. Capacity qualification (FRZ-PRD-11, PROD-Q) is OPEN, so no closed stage is invalidated.
recommendation: Fail closed (or mark capacity unqualified in diagnostics) when a PRODUCT/STRICT host has production adapters enabled and backend kind is in_memory; reconcile ELASTIC doc line 179 with wiring.

title: Queue worker wiring downgrades Kafka/RabbitMQ to in-process eager Celery with memory broker, also in STRICT hosts
affected_invariant: FRZ-REL-07 no hidden fallback; BACKGROUND_TASKS: eager Celery stacks are test/eval only
impact: INTERGRAX_QUEUE_BACKEND=kafka|rabbitmq is silently rewritten to CELERY and the worker app is built with memory:// broker and task_always_eager=True regardless of production_mode, so STRICT hosts with include_queue_worker (default False) run work in-process, not through a broker. BACKGROUND_TASKS.md classifies eager Celery as TEST/EVAL ONLY; the env var is in no doc or test and no test covers the downgrade (grep over tests/applications). Default hosts (inline backend) are unaffected.
recommendation: Raise on KAFKA/RABBITMQ (or when production_mode is true) instead of rewriting; document INTERGRAX_QUEUE_BACKEND; add a negative test.

title: Nexus-internal HITL decision persistence is a silent no-op in the production Nexus construction
affected_invariant: RELIABILITY_FAILURE_AND_HITL: approve/reject/escalate decisions go through the decision store
impact: persist_human_decision returns without writing when human_store is None; NexusLoop.human_decision_store defaults to None and environment_orchestration_materialization.py (the only non-debug NexusLoop construction) passes no store and the application wiring applier names none. So reject/escalate verdicts handled inside Nexus are not persisted by that path; the SQLite store is composed only for tool-provider/debug consumers. Whether another durable path records the verdict was not verified. Missing HITL still never approves (FRZ-GOV-06 unaffected by this code).
recommendation: Campaign B: trace a reject/escalate run end to end and check durable decision evidence; if lost, inject the store in materialization or fail closed in STRICT.
